details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorm activity is increasing within the warm advection regime across portions of eastern Iowa into northern Illinois/Indiana. This activity is ongoing north of a surface front extending from the central Plains across southern Illinois into southern Illinois/northern Kentucky. The air mass near the ongoing convection is only marginally unstable located on the northern fringes of more moderate to strong instability further south across southern Illinois into portions of southern Indiana/northern Kentucky. Forecast soundings suggest the presence of a fairly strong cap at the base of the EML across much of the region of greater buoyancy, which will likely inhibit surface based convection. Generally boundary parallel flow will likely produce training storms overnight, with little organized severe potential. Later into the overnight/early morning, the low-level jet will increase into Illinois/Indiana. Should a cluster be able to develop and drop southward, there could be some damaging wind potential into the morning. A few instances of gusty winds and small hail will be possible with stronger cores. For now, confidence in a more organized severe risk remains low but trends will be monitored overnight
